jobs.description: Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) is a service that enables sellers to outsource supply chain and fulfillment to Amazon and use Amazon’s world-class technology, science and logistics infrastructure to deliver billions of products from manufacturing hubs to customer doorsteps worldwide with a fast delivery promise. The first twenty years of FBA made world-class fulfillment accessible to any seller. Our next chapter is about making speed accessible, giving sellers the tools, transparency, and control to deliver faster, in ways that make economic sense for their business. As the leader of Fast Delivery Programs product management, you will own the worldwide strategy for how sellers participate in Amazon's fastest delivery channels across North America, Europe, India, Latin America, and the Middle East. Customers increasingly expect delivery in hours, not days, and the categories driving that growth are where third-party sellers bring the depth and breadth customers need. But sub-same-day and quick commerce delivery are fundamentally different from the core fulfillment network. Selection is physically constrained, capacity is scarce, and every slot at a fast-delivery site has a cost. Deciding which products earn that space, which sellers get capacity, and what it should cost them is a new kind of product problem. Solving it means combining Amazon's algorithms with sellers' own demand signals. Your portfolio spans the full breadth of fast delivery: defining the worldwide speed strategy that governs how sellers participate in delivery speed across a portfolio of programs; designing and scaling mechanisms that allocate scarce capacity at speed nodes to sellers; building fee structures and seller incentive frameworks that align seller economics with network cost structures; optimizing product selection for capacity-constrained sites; designing seller-facing programs, communications, and workflows; and launching fast delivery programs architected from day one for worldwide scale. You'll start by leading a team of product and program managers, and partner with science and engineering to turn optimization and market mechanism design into products sellers use every day to grow their business and make money. We're looking for a leader who builds. You'll set the vision and develop a strong PM team, and you'll still get hands-on: prototyping new seller experiences and pricing concepts with AI tools, putting working versions in front of sellers and leaders within days, and making that the team's default way of working. The portfolio has grown into parallel tracks spanning supply chain, operations, delivery experience, fulfillment technology, and finance. Your job is to turn that into one coherent roadmap and shipped products with measurable positive seller outcomes. Key job responsibilities – Define the multi-year vision and worldwide roadmap for FBA fast delivery. Work backwards from customers' expectation of delivery in hours to expand selection, improve speed, and lower cost to serve. – Define how sellers participate in sub-same-day and quick commerce delivery channels across all geographies. – Design the end-to-end marketplace framework for fast delivery, spanning selection for limited shelf space, capacity allocation, inbound and inventory paths, seller recommendations and tools, and fee and incentive structures that align seller economics with customer outcomes. – Build seller-facing programs, tools, and communications that give sellers transparency, control, and a clear path to grow through faster delivery. – Partner with science and engineering to turn optimization models, market designs and seller insights into product features. Set technical direction and priorities and make architecture and scope tradeoffs. – Prototype new concepts yourself using AI coding, design and analysis tools. Validate ideas with working versions rather than long specs and build the same habits across your team. – Hire, lead, and develop a team of product and program managers and set a high bar for technical product ownership and engineering partnership. – Define the metrics framework for fast delivery (customer impact, seller outcomes, program health), and use it to drive investment decisions with VP-level leaders across supply chain, operations, seller and customer experience, and delivery. A day in the life One morning you might be working through how limited capacity at a new sub-same-day site should be split among thousands of sellers who all want in, and what it should cost them. By afternoon you could be demoing a working prototype of a seller capacity-request flow you built with AI tools, reviewing pilot results from a newly launched country, or coaching a PM through a tradeoff between speed and cost to serve. Your decisions will shape how millions of sellers reach Amazon's fastest delivery channels, and how billions of dollars in fulfillment investment turn into outcomes for customers and sellers. About the team FBA gives third-party sellers an end-to-end supply chain, from manufacturing sites to customers' doorsteps, so they can focus on growing their businesses. The team owns warehousing, inventory, fulfillment, pricing, and the recommendations that help sellers make the right decisions. We work closely with sellers to understand their experience, build agentic solutions for them, design seller policies and incentives, and develop products that help sellers and Amazon together delight customers worldwide. We also build the systems that manage inbound, transportation, and storage capacity, design a network that increases speed while reducing cost to serve, and run voice-of-seller systems that build seller trust. We are open to hiring candidates to work out of one of the following locations: Bellevue, WA, or Sunnyvale, CA.

jobs.description: WHAT YOU'LL DO We're looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer for Midjourney Medical — from precision electromechanical assemblies up to the large-scale structures and mechanisms that hold everything together and make it move. This role spans the full range of scale: one week you might be refining a compact transducer mount, the next you're architecting a structural frame or designing the motion system that positions hardware within it. This is a hands-on role on a small cross-functional team. You'll take problems from whiteboard sketch to working hardware yourself — designing in CAD, prototyping in the shop, testing, iterating, and integrating with research teams, electrical and software engineers along the way. We move fast and expect you to drive your own work: identifying what needs to happen next, making sound engineering calls without waiting for permission, and shipping hardware that works. - Own parts of the mechanical systems end to end — structures, mechanisms, and electromechanical integration - Design large-scale structures: frames, weldments, enclosures, and support systems, with attention to stiffness, weight, manufacturability, and serviceability - Design mechanisms: linkages, motion stages, actuation systems for precise, reliable positioning and articulation - Integrate transducers, electronics, cabling, and thermal management into large physical systems - Perform engineering analysis (tolerance stack-ups, structural/FEA, mechanism kinematics) to de-risk designs before committing to hardware - Build and test relentlessly — 3D printing, rapid prototyping, and hands-on fabrication are core to how you'll validate designs - Select parts and materials for system-level integration, balancing performance, cost, and lead time - Drive projects independently from concept through validation, and collaborate closely with a small cross-disciplinary team to hit project goals WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field - 5+ years of experience designing and shipping electromechanical hardware - Demonstrated track record in mechanism design — you can point to mechanisms you've designed that work reliably in the real world - Experience designing larger-scale structures (frames, gantries, enclosures, or similar), not just component-level parts - Proficiency in CAD (we use OnShape) for design, optimization, and system integration - Strong rapid-prototyping experience — this is a must; you should be as comfortable in the shop as at your desk - Background in R&D environments where the problem isn't fully defined and the path forward is yours to figure out - Excellent creative problem-solving and analytical skills - Experience working closely with a small cross-disciplinary team

The Instrumentation Controls and Electrical (ICE) Supervisor is responsible for leading and coordinating Instrumentation, Controls, and Electrical maintenance activities across production and water facilities. This position oversees ICE technicians, corrective and preventative maintenance, routine calibrations, safety shutdown systems, equipment reliability, training, and work scheduling through Maximo.
The role works closely with Operations, Water, Production Control Center, Completions, Internal Gas Measurement, SCADA, Automation, Engineering, and other support groups to ensure facilities are maintained safely, reliably, and efficiently throughout their operating lifecycle.
The Instrumentation Controls and Electrical (ICE) Supervisor responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Leadership
Coordinate and prioritize corrective maintenance activities with ICE technicians.
Support troubleshooting of instrumentation, electrical, controls, communications, measurement, and safety systems.
Manage emergency and high-priority maintenance response.
Identify recurring failures and drive long-term corrective actions.
Ensure maintenance activities are completed safely, efficiently, and properly documented.
Planning and Scheduling
Schedule and manage technician work through Maximo.
Prioritize work based on safety, production impact, equipment criticality, and operational needs.
Maintain visibility of open work orders, backlog, overdue work, and completion status.
Coordinate maintenance around outages, completions activity, facility startups, and operational priorities.
Preventative Maintenance and Calibration
Establish, maintain, and continuously improve the ICE preventative maintenance program.
Ensure routine instrumentation calibrations are completed at required frequencies.
Maintain PM and calibration requirements for critical production and water facility equipment.
Monitor PM compliance and correct overdue or ineffective maintenance activities.
Use equipment history and failure trends to improve maintenance strategies.
Safety Systems
Oversee inspection, testing, calibration, and maintenance of facility safety and shutdown systems.
Ensure transmitters, switches, alarms, trips, interlocks, and emergency shutdown devices are maintained and tested.
Coordinate safety system testing with Operations, PCC, SCADA, and other affected groups.
Ensure deficiencies in critical protective systems are corrected promptly.
Production and Water Facility Support
Oversee ICE maintenance for production gas and water facilities.
Support instrumentation, electrical, controls, communications, measurement, pumps, tanks, and associated field equipment.
Coordinate with Water, Completions, Internal Gas Measurement, SCADA, and Operations.
Support facility commissioning, startup, shutdown, outage, reactivation, and transition into long-term operations.
Electrical Safety and NFPA 70E
Oversee ICE electrical maintenance activities up to and including 480 VAC within the approved scope of the department.
Ensure technicians are trained, qualified, and authorized for the electrical work they perform.
Ensure ICE technicians maintain required NFPA 70E training and qualifications.
Coordinate initial and refresher electrical safety training as required.
Reinforce safe electrical work practices, including lockout/tagout, absence-of-voltage verification, proper PPE, approach boundaries, and arc-flash requirements.
Maintain awareness of technician qualifications and ensure personnel work within their authorized level of training.
Equipment Lifecycle Management
Maintain ICE equipment standards throughout the lifecycle of production and water facilities.
Ensure equipment is properly documented in Maximo with asset records, specifications, PM requirements, calibration frequencies, and maintenance history.
Identify obsolete, unreliable, or unsupported equipment and coordinate replacement.
Provide maintenance input during equipment selection, construction, commissioning, and facility modifications.
Work with Automation, Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain to improve equipment standardization.
Technician Leadership and Development
Provide direct leadership, coaching, and technical support to ICE technicians.
Establish training plans based on equipment, safety requirements, technology, and identified skill gaps.
Coordinate vendor and manufacturer training where needed.
Develop technician capabilities in instrumentation, electrical, controls, SCADA, communications, measurement, calibration, and troubleshooting.
Promote accountability, consistent work practices, and strong equipment ownership.
Reliability and Continuous Improvement
Review equipment failures and maintenance history to identify reliability improvements.
Support root cause investigations and corrective actions for significant or repeat failures.
Track key maintenance metrics including PM compliance, calibration compliance, backlog, repeat failures, emergency work, and equipment reliability.
Identify opportunities to reduce downtime, repeat work, and operating cost.

High school diploma or equivalent.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in instrumentation, electrical, controls, automation, industrial maintenance, oil and gas operations, or a related technical field.
Experience troubleshooting and maintaining industrial instrumentation and electrical equipment.
Working knowledge of electrical systems up to 480 VAC.
Knowledge of preventative maintenance, calibration, and safety shutdown systems.
Familiarity with NFPA 70E and electrical safe work practices.
Experience with Maximo or a similar maintenance management system.
Strong leadership, planning, scheduling, communication, and organizational skills.
Ability to read electrical drawings, P&IDs, control drawings, and technical documentation.
Preferred Experience and Skills
Associate or bachelor's degree in Electrical Technology, Instrumentation, Automation, Electronics, Engineering Technology, Industrial Maintenance, or a related field.
Previous supervisory or lead technician experience.
Oil and gas production or water facility maintenance experience.
Experience with PLCs, RTUs, SCADA, industrial communications, gas measurement, transmitters, control valves, and electrical distribution.
Experience developing training programs and maintenance standards.
Current NFPA 70E training preferred.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. This is a national role anchored in the National Capital Region, supporting the Government of Canada, provincial/territorial governments, Canada's national security and defence community, crown corporations, and the broader public sector.

Drive new business and revenue growth across the Canadian public sector, with the Government of Canada as the primary focus and provincial/territorial governments, crown corporations, and the broader public sector as secondary coverage, owning the full sales cycle from initial outreach through deployment
